findings.reason: item 3 fixes `estimate_ms` to "time the context estimate ... wherever it runs", and clause 1's test asserts one `estimate_ms` for the pick; with the site-mapping wrong, an implementer cannot tell which of the two runs on the shadow path the stage should record (or that the pre-pick run is the one dispatch actually pays for), so the seam the done-when tests is underspecified.
findings.text: §12 states `estimated_context_tokens` "runs at two sites. On the shadow path it runs in `reckon/crew/dispatch_picker.py` before `pick()` starts ... On the direct path it runs inside `candidates()`", but `pick()` calls `snapshot.candidates` (the default `snapshotter`, `reckon/crew/picker/__init__.py:202,236-243`) on every pick, and `candidates()` calls `estimated_context_tokens` unconditionally at `snapshot.py:696-698`; so `dispatch_picker.py:251` is an *extra* pre-pick call on the shadow path, not the shadow path's alternative to `candidates()` — the shadow path runs the estimate twice, once untimed outside the pick and once inside `snapshot_ms`.

findings.reason: the discrepancy is a snapshot/denominator slip on a non-load-bearing figure; the tail attribution, the exemption clause, and every done-when clause are unaffected.
findings.text: §12's cited figures do not reconcile with the file it cites: it reports "55 of 246 production picks" and "`capability_ms` runs 1.4 s median on the 52 picks that record it", but `capability_ms` first appears at row 215 of `pick-timings.jsonl`, so a 246-row set cannot hold 52 capability records; the 52-record figure matches row 267, where the over-bound count is 57 (not 55) and the whole-pick median is 1.42 s (not 1.5 s). The distinctive maxima do match (latency 21 s, `snapshot_ms` 10.5 s, `state_render_ms` 17.3 s at n=267).
